- dbe-tool sql: selecting typeof(col) without an aggregate errors; wrap it in any_value(). EXPLAIN ANALYZE works.
  Bash: only plain dbe-tool calls; no cd, shell variables, pipes, or chained commands.

- G1R1: E0001 per-group simple_update in perfect HT -> RETIRED (bad idea: groups interleaved, partitioning costs more).
- G1R2: E0002 bitpacking select (flat compacted payload) -> RETIRED: neutral. Slicing is not the cost.
- G1R3: E0003 perfect HT replicate states K=4 -> ACCEPTED, -12.3% geomean (1.140x). HT CPU 1.50 -> 1.37s; so chain latency

- Perfect HT: K=8 replicas; drop the 8 AddInPlace passes (per-aggregate offset), or fuse sum/avg loops into one pass.
- Fuse stacked projections (in backlog; needs investigation of compressed_materialization). ~0.44s CPU in projections.
- Bitpacking `filter` callback (filter while decompressing). The date filter alone costs 71ms, so the gain is limited.
- Decimal multiply overflow checks in projections (could skip using stats).
- Scan is the largest operator (2.06s); no single anomaly found yet. Old Dictionary select callback is untried.

issues.title: avg on int32/int64/decimal(int64): int64 sum state when stats prove no overflow
issues.hypothesis: PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY is 1.41s CPU on q01 (second-largest operator after the 2.06s scan). 3 of its 8 aggregates are avg over DECIMAL(15,2) (int64 physical). These use AvgState<hugeint_t> with AddToHugeint::AddValue (extension/core_functions/include/core_functions/aggregate/sum_helpers.hpp:109), which costs a 128-bit add, an overflow compare and a branch per row, plus a 32-byte state instead of 16 bytes. The 4 sums are already rewritten to sum_no_overflow (int64 state) by SumPropagateStats (sum.cpp:126) when |min|,|max| * max_cardinality fits int64, but avg has no such statistics callback. The same rewrite for avg turns 3 of 8 scatter loops into plain int64 adds and makes the state tuple smaller (better cache use, cheaper replicas from E0003).
issues.plan: In extension/core_functions/aggregate/algebraic/avg.cpp: (1) add `struct IntegerAverageOperationInt64 : BaseSumOperation<AverageSetOperation, RegularAdd>` whose Finalize is bit-identical to IntegerAverageOperationHugeint: `long double divident = GetAverageDivident<long double>(count, bind_data); target = Hugeint::Cast<long double>(hugeint_t(state.value)) / divident;` (go through hugeint_t so the rounding matches exactly on every platform). (2) add `AvgPropagateStats(ClientContext&, BoundAggregateExpression &expr, AggregateStatisticsInput &input)` modelled on SumPropagateStats: require input.node_stats->has_max_cardinality and NumericStats::HasMinMax(child_stats[0]); internal type INT32 or INT64 only; compute max/min * max_cardinality in hugeint; if both are strictly inside int64 bounds, build `AggregateFunction::UnaryAggregate<AvgState<int64_t>, INPUT, double, IntegerAverageOperationInt64>(arg_type, DOUBLE)` and copy name, arguments, return type, bind callback (keep expr.bind_info untouched — the decimal scale stays), and set NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT; clear its statistics callback; assign to expr.function. Return nullptr. (3) attach the callback (SetStatisticsCallback) to the INT32 and INT64 variants in GetAverageAggregateInternal, which also covers BindDecimalAvg for decimals with int32/int64 storage. Leave INT16 (already int64 state), INT128, interval, time types untouched. Check that a plan serialised after the rewrite (if any) still deserialises: keeping name 'avg' + bind re-run yields the hugeint version, which gives the same results.
issues.expected_gain: q01: 3-7% (3 of 8 aggregates in the 1.41s perfect-HT operator get cheaper; state tuple shrinks by ~48 bytes).
issues.generality: Any avg over INTEGER/BIGINT/DECIMAL(<=18) columns with min/max stats (most scans of base tables), in perfect HT, hash aggregate and ungrouped aggregate. Nothing should get slower; when stats are missing or too wide, the hugeint path is kept.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness depends on the bound check (copy the sum one exactly) and on the finalize being bit-identical (use the hugeint cast). Make sure the swapped function keeps the bind data and the result type DOUBLE.
